Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT or THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagrnahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF TIRE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 24 April 26, 2006 MR. HAI SOY S. TAN Unique Agri-Commercial Corporation Captain Cooper Street, San Jose Occidental Mindoro Dear Mr. Tan: This has reference to your earlier letter seeking our legal opinion concerning the extent of the powers of the Sangguniang Bayan to reclassify lands, the extent of the review power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, and the consequence of non-compliance by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan with the reglementary period requirement within which to review Sannguniang Bayan ordinances. Per your letter, Unique Agri-Commercial Corporation (UACC) applied for a development permit with the Municipality of San Jose, Occidental Mindoro for its Saint Virginia's Memorial Garden (SVMG) project with its site at Barangay Bubog of said municipality. UACC was required by the Municipal Planning and Development Coordinator to secure from the Sangguniang Bayan a reclassification (agricultural to non-agricultural) of the lot where SVMG project has to be undertaken. Accordingly, Ordinance No. 697, s. 04, was passed on February 9, 2004, entitled "An Ordinance Reclassifying from Agricultural to Non-agricultural use a Parcel of Land containing an Area of 40,961 Square Meters, located in Barangay Bubog, this Municipality, titled under TCT No. T- 13737, described as Lot No. 1633-B-7 of the Subdivision Plan PSD-04-088174 in the name of Unique Agri-Commercial Corporation represented by Mr. Hai Soy Tan". Said ordinance was transmitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review on February 25, 2004. In its Resolution dated August 2, 2004, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan disapproved the aforesaid ordinance citing the following as reasons which we shall quote in toto: 1. The topographical characteristics is not suited for cemetery considering the shallow water level, and that converting the same as cemetery site might contaminate the water within the 6

-2- area to the detriment of health conditions of people residing within the vicinity. 2. Considering that the adjacent lands are presently being used for agricultural production, conversion of said lot into a cemetery may result to economic dislocation of farmers in the area; 3. Reclassification of Zand should adhere conform with approved comprehensive land use plan of the municipality" In response thereto, the UACC filed a request for reconsideration of the foregoing disapproval to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. The latter body, in turn, indorsed UACC's request for reconsideration to the Sangguniang Bayan for comment. The Sangguniang Bayan recommended to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan that said request for reconsideration be given a favorable response. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan nevertheless denied UACC's request for reconsideration. Hence, you now seek our legal opinion on the following issues, which we reproduced in toto from your letter: 1) "Does the Sangguniang Bayan acted within the scope of its authority when it enacted the said Municipal Ordinance reclassifying a parcel of land without taking into consideration other laws, rules and regulations and policies that are national in scope which govemed the processes in memorial park project? 2) The legal effects on the failure of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to act zvithin thirty (30) day period as required by law for the review of Sangguniang Bayan Ordinance No. 697, series of 2004. 3) Are we in estoppel for having written the Sangguniang Panlalawigan upon the directive of the Sangguniang Bayan after the thirty (30) day limitation as imposed by Section 56 of the Local Government Code of 1991? 4) Does the Sangguniang Panlalawigan acted within the scope of its authority when it conducted functions belonging to Sangguniang Bayan such as public consultations, hearing and entertaining petitioners during the review of said Municipal Ordinance?

-3- 5) Are the processes conducted by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan beyond the thirty (30) day limitation valid or has no effect at In reply to your first query, may we invite your attention to Section 447 (a) (2) (x) of the Local Government Code (RA 7160) and we quote: "SECTION 447. Powers, Duties, Functions, and Compensation.- (a) The sanggunian bayan xxx shall: XXX xxx xxx (x) Subject to national law, process and approve subdivision plans for residential, commercial, or industrial purposes and other development purposes xxx". (Emphasis Supplied) While the duty to process and the power to approve subdivision plans for commercial and other development purposes are vested with the sanggunian, the exercise of the same, however, must conform to national law. It is to be noted that the subject municipal ordinance was enacted purposely as a requirement for memorial park project. A reading of the HLURB Rules and Regulations for Memorial Parks and Cemeteries and the Department of Agrarian Reform Rules and Regulations pertinent thereto provide no such requirement. Hence, such reclassification requirement through an ordinance is in the nature of an additional requirement on memorial park project on top of those required by existing rules and regulations of national agencies. Relevantly, a case in point is the case of Villacorta YS- Bernardo (143 SCRA 480), the Supreme Court held that additional conditions upon subdivisions owners are null and void. Ordinances amending and so violating national laws in the guise of implementing them are ultra vires. In reply to your second query, may we invite your attention to Section 56 of the Local Government Code and we quote: "SECTION 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. — (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. xxx

-4- (d) If no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid." (Emphasis supplied) The review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan may bring out either the declaration of validity or invalidity of an ordinance or resolution approving local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development council. The declaration of validity may come in two (2) modes, namely, a) as a consequence of substantial review; b) as a consequence of inaction. In the latter case, if no action has been taken by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of the ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid (Section 56). Hence, there are two concurring duties incumbent upon the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to do, and these are: a) to review the ordinance or subject resolution as to its substance; and b) to review the same within the 30-day period. As to the former, there can be no doubt as to its mandatory nature. As held in Vda. De Mesa uS. Mencias (G.R. No. L-24583, October 29, 1966), "Where the statute provides for the doing of some act which is required by justice or public duty, or where it invests a public body, municipality or public officer with power and authority to take some action which concerns the public interest or rights of individuals, the permissive language will be construed as mandatory and the execution of the power may be insisted as a duty" As to the latter, the general rule is "Where a statute prescribes a time within which a public officer is to perform official acts affecting the rights of others, it is directory as to the time, unless from the nature of the act the designation of time must be considered a limitation on the power of the officer" (50 Am Jur-, 23, p.46 cited by Alcantara, Samson in his book Statutes, 1990 Ed.). It is very evident from the last paragraph of Section 56 (d) that the designation of the 30-day period serves as a limitation on the power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Members to review a municipal ordinance or resolution. It explicitly says that if no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. Accordingly, the 30-day period prescribed by law within which for the Sanggunian Panlalawigan to act on review of municipal ordinances should be construed as mandatory. Moreover, from the point of view of public policy and

-5- interest, if we construe the period to be merely directory, this would render municipal ordinances unstable and may even result to the subservience of the lower sanggunian to the higher sanggunian since the latter could still act on review at anytime it pleases and may whimsically or arbitrarily disapprove the ordinance anytime to the prejudice of the lower LGU who may have already implemented the subject ordinance for quite sometime. Corollarily, the ordinance having been presumed to be valid, discussion on your third and fifth queries becomes irrelevant. In reply to your fourth query, we answer in the negative. Please be informed that in the case of Moday CA (268 SCRA 586), the Supreme Court, citing Velasco Blas (115 SCRA 540) held and we quote: "The only ground upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, ordinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance, or order is 'beyond the powers conferred upon the council or president making the same.' Absolutely no other ground is recognized by the law. A strictly legal question is before the provincial board in its consideration of a municipal resolution, ordinance, or order. The provincial (board's) disapproval of any resolution, ordinance, or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance, or order is outside the scope of the legal powers conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limits, it usurps the legislative functions of the municipal council or president. Such has been the consistent course of executive authority." (Emphasis Supplied) We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. w Legal: 17/Merle cc.: THE REGIONAL DIRECTOR DILG, Region IV-B 3M Floor Santos & Sons Building 973 Aurora Boulevard cor. Dapdap Street Cubao, Quezon City ly yours, CEUTO T. ANDANA Undersecreta
